anchor._note: An old sunken anchor about 1.2 m long: an eight-sided shank tapering up from a rounded crown, two arms curving up from the crown, each ending in a spade-shaped fluke, a stock across near the top, and a ring at the top; rusty brown. Built standing; the map lays it over, half in the sand. Written by tools/models/scenery.py.
anchor.name: Anchor

anemone._note: A sea anemone about 380 mm across and 300 mm tall: a squat twelve-sided column on a wider foot, a flat oral disc on top dipping to the mouth in its middle, and two rings of thick, blunt, tapering six-sided tentacles round the disc's rim, twelve long ones outside and six shorter inside, curving out then up, pale at the tips. The tentacles wave in the current (sway, 3 s round). Written by tools/models/scenery.py.
anemone.name: Sea anemone

board-stand-in._note: A plain flat stand-in for the board while the real board model is made: a slab 3150 mm square and 40 mm tall (15 squares of 210 mm), its top in two pale shades by square so the squares read. Square (row r, column c) has its middle at x = (c - 7) * 210, z = (r - 7) * 210. A box because a board is one. Written by tools/models/marks_scenes.py.
board-stand-in.name: Board stand-in

board._note: The board: 15 x 15 squares of 210 mm on a wooden slab whose top, where tiles sit, is at y = 40; each square a 202 mm plate between 8 mm grooves 5 mm deep, inside a rim 74 mm wide standing 10 mm over the squares. Square (row r, column c), both 0 to 14, has its centre at x = (c - 7) * 210, z = (r - 7) * 210 (the centre square is the origin; row 0 is the far edge, -z). The standard premium layout, as (row,col): 2L: 0,3 0,11 2,6 2,8 3,0 3,7 3,14 6,2 6,6 6,8 6,12 7,3 7,11 8,2 8,6 8,8 8,12 11,0 11,7 11,14 12,6 12,8 14,3 14,11; 2W: 1,1 1,13 2,2 2,12 3,3 3,11 4,4 4,10 7,7 10,4 10,10 11,3 11,11 12,2 12,12 13,1 13,13; 3L: 1,5 1,9 5,1 5,5 5,9 5,13 9,1 9,5 9,9 9,13 13,5 13,9; 3W: 0,0 0,7 0,14 7,0 7,14 14,0 14,7 14,14. The centre (7,7) is a double word marked by a star. Each other premium is stamped with its label (3W, 2W, 3L, 2L), white on the triple squares and brown on the double ones, so colour is not the only cue. The premium colours keep clear of the four player colours. Written by tools/models/world.py.
board.name: Board

bottle._note: A glass bottle about 380 mm long lying on its side, sunk a third into the sand: a twelve-sided round body, a sloping shoulder and a narrow neck with a lip, sea-green glass with a paler shine along it, and a cork in the mouth. Written by tools/models/scenery.py.
bottle.name: Bottle

boulder._note: A rounded seafloor boulder about 640 mm across and 400 mm high, sunk a little into the sand: a squashed, jittered ball of flat facets in three grey-greens. Written by tools/models/world.py.
boulder.name: Boulder

coral-brain._note: A brain coral, a low dome about 840 mm across and 260 mm over the sand, sunk a little: twenty-four sides and nine bands, coloured in winding ridges and grooves. Written by tools/models/scenery.py.
coral-brain.name: Brain coral

coral-staghorn._note: A staghorn coral about 1 m across and 0.6 m tall: five short trunks from the sand forking again and again into round, tapering six-sided branches that curve upward, with pale growing tips. Written by tools/models/scenery.py.
coral-staghorn.name: Staghorn coral

crab._note: The crab every player steers, its shell in the player's colour (SECOND-ORDER R1.90). Anatomy of a green or blue shore crab, checked from above, the side, the front and 3/4: a carapace wider than long (90 mm across the teeth, 86 behind them, 69 long; under half a tile across), widest across its front third just behind the eyes, five teeth on each front-side margin, tapering to a narrower back edge, gently domed; two eyes on short stalks in notches at the front middle, short antennae between them; two claws from the front corners under the shell, each an arm (merus), a wrist (carpus) and a big palm (propodus, 30 mm long, 22 deep and up to 21 broad, a swollen teardrop section; the heaviest limbs) with a stout toothed fixed finger below and a movable finger (dactyl) hinged on top, folded in front of the face with the palms turned 22 degrees in (idle, walks, jump; hold, grab and place turn them straight so a held tile sits square); four pairs of walking legs from under the sides, splayed sideways (about 150 mm tip to tip), the upper segment (merus) flattened and broad, each rising from under the margin to a high knee above the shell and angling down to a pointed tip, bending in the plane across the body, the back pair swept back with paddle-flat tips as a swimming crab's; the abdomen a broad rounded flap folded flat under the body, about 38 mm wide. A tile (200 mm) is bigger than the crab; a held one is drawn at half size (look.json held). Parts: body; eye_l, eye_r; claw_l_arm, claw_l_wrist, claw_l_palm, claw_l_finger and claw_r_...; leg_l1_hip, leg_l1_knee, leg_l1_foot for left legs 1 (front) to 4 (back) and leg_r1_... on the right, each named after the joint it turns about (hip: coxa and merus up to the knee; knee: carpus and propodus down to the ankle; foot: the dactyl). Anchors claw_left and claw_right: the middle of a held tile's underside, the tile's near edge between the open fingers (a 9 mm gap at rest). The walks go toward +x (walk_side) and +z (walk_fwd); played backwards they go the other way. The jump is the crab's pose only; the game lifts it. Written by tools/models/crab.py.
crab.name: Crab

fish._note: A school of four small fish, the Title's fish (title-fish, tools/models/title_models.py) copied at 85 to 115%: they swim nose first round a loop 3.2 m across about 0.9 m over the sand, once every 24 s, tails beating and bodies wagging a little against them (sway). The middle of the model is the loop's middle. Written by tools/models/scenery.py from title-fish.json; regenerate after the Title's fish changes.
fish.name: Fish

ghost-tile._note: The ghost tile: a held tile's see-through copy on the square a click would place it. The same shape and labels as data/models/tile.json (200 x 200 x 45 mm, origin the middle of its underside), in see-through sea-glass aqua so it reads as not placed yet against the wooden tiles and the sand; its face glows a little. Copied from tile.json by the tools/models/marks_scenes.py: keep its vertices in step with tile.json.
ghost-tile.name: Ghost tile

kelp._note: Giant kelp, 1.8 to 2.4 m tall: a holdfast of five root-like haptera knotted on the sand, two tapering six-sided stipes rising from it, each in five segments; two long ribbed blades a segment lean out and up from round gas bladders, on alternate sides, longer toward the top. The stipes sway in the current, more toward the top (sway, 4.8 s round). Written by tools/models/scenery.py.
kelp.name: Kelp

light-shaft._note: A soft shaft of sunlight from the surface: two nested slanting eight-sided tubes 7 m tall, narrow at the top and spreading toward the sand, see-through and unlit (glow), stopping a little over the sand. Drawn each frame with the other see-through things. Written by tools/models/scenery.py.
light-shaft.name: Light shaft

mound-dome._note: A low sand mound, a domed heap: 2.3 by 2.1 m and 340 mm high, a soft cosine dome with a wobbly outline, gentle enough for a crab to walk up (under 25 degrees). Tiles are found in piles on the mounds. Its rim is sunk 30 mm under the floor. Written by tools/models/world.py; tools/piles.py lays tiles on these very faces.
mound-dome.name: Mound, domed

mound-long._note: A low sand mound, a long ridge: 3.3 by 1.8 m and 300 mm high, a soft cosine dome with a wobbly outline, gentle enough for a crab to walk up (under 25 degrees). Tiles are found in piles on the mounds. Its rim is sunk 30 mm under the floor. Written by tools/models/world.py; tools/piles.py lays tiles on these very faces.
mound-long.name: Mound, long

mound-low._note: A low sand mound, a wide, low swell: 2.8 by 2.6 m and 200 mm high, a soft cosine dome with a wobbly outline, gentle enough for a crab to walk up (under 25 degrees). Tiles are found in piles on the mounds. Its rim is sunk 30 mm under the floor. Written by tools/models/world.py; tools/piles.py lays tiles on these very faces.
mound-low.name: Mound, low

pebble._note: A pebble about 180 mm across, for scattering by the rocks. Written by tools/models/world.py.
pebble.name: Pebble

rock-flat._note: A flat seafloor rock about 900 by 620 mm and 240 mm high, a slab worn smooth. Written by tools/models/world.py.
rock-flat.name: Rock, flat

sand-patch._note: A patch of seafloor sand 8 m across, for the Gallery and for scenes: a low, gently uneven disc of flat facets in three sand shades, its rim sunk 40 mm under the floor so its edge never shows. The origin is its middle, on the floor. Written by tools/models/starters.py.
sand-patch.name: Sand patch

scallop._note: A scallop shell, about 340 mm across: a domed round fan of eleven low ribs fanning from the hinge to a scalloped edge, cupped side up, with the two ears at the hinge; coral and cream. Cartoon-big beside a 200 mm tile. Written by tools/models/world.py.
scallop.name: Scallop

sea-fan._note: A sea fan (a gorgonian) about 1.1 m across and 1 m tall: a short six-sided stem and, from its top, three ribs fanning out in one flat plane, each forking three times into thinner tapering ribs, the fine net between them a flat fan behind. Written by tools/models/scenery.py.
sea-fan.name: Sea fan

seafloor._note: The seafloor the board lies on: a low-poly disc of sand 38 m across, flat within 2 m of the middle (under the board and the crabs' corners), rolling a few centimetres out to the mounds, then into low dunes that the fog takes; its rim sunk 60 mm under the floor. Triangles in three sand shades. Written by tools/models/world.py; tools/piles.py lays tiles on these very faces.
seafloor.name: Seafloor

starfish._note: A starfish, about 430 mm across: five plump tapering arms, each a low ridge, round a domed middle; orange with a paler top. Written by tools/models/world.py.
starfish.name: Starfish

tile._note: A wooden letter tile, 200 x 200 x 45 mm on the board's 210 mm squares (SECOND-ORDER R1.8): a slab with rounded corners, its top and bottom edges chamfered, lighter on its face than on its sides, the face in strips of two close shades for a faint grain running up the letter, like a real wooden word tile (about 4.4 times as wide as it is thick). The origin is the middle of its underside. Its labels: the letter in the middle of the face, a little up and left, and the point value in the bottom right corner as read (the letter's up is -z). Written by tools/models/starters.py.
tile.name: Tile

title-bubble._note: A rising bubble for the title card, 100 mm across (scale it per bubble): a ball of 12 sides by 7 rings, see-through and glowing pale aqua so it reads as air in water, with a small solid fleck of shine up and to the front. It stands on y = 0 (its middle is 50 up). Written by tools/models/title_models.py.
title-bubble.name: Bubble

title-fish._note: A small cartoon fish for the title card, about 200 mm nose to tail, swimming nose first along +z with its middle 60 mm up: a deep flattened oval body (taller than wide, widest a third back from the nose, a darker back and pale belly) tapering to a thin tail stalk, a forked tail fin that swishes side to side (sway, 0.9 s round), a dorsal fin, a belly fin, a pectoral fin and a dark eye each side. Written by tools/models/title_models.py.
title-fish.name: Fish

title-scallop._note: A scallop shell lying on the sand for the title card, cartoon big (about 170 mm across, 150 front to back; a real one is 50-150 mm): a low fan-shaped dome with radiating ribs (ridges and grooves in two coral shades) opening to the front (+z), its hinge at the back with the two flat ears (auricles) either side, as on a real scallop. Written by tools/models/title_models.py.
title-scallop.name: Scallop shell

weed._note: A tuft of sea weed: five broad ribbon blades 0.6 to 1 m tall leaning out from one root, each in four segments that bend more toward the tip as it sways in the current (sway, 3.6 s round). Written by tools/models/world.py.
weed.name: Weed

whelk._note: A spiral sea shell lying on its side, about 390 mm long: a big body whorl tapering through bumpy whorls to a pointed spire, cream with a brown band winding round it and a pink mouth. Written by tools/models/world.py.
whelk.name: Spiral shell
